applicability: Applies to expressions with 1 to 8 integer operands each in [-10,20] and exactly len(operands)-1 operators drawn from '+', '-', '*'. Rejects malformed inputs, booleans, out-of-range operands, wrong operator counts, and unknown operators via ValueError. Complexity is O(n^3 * S^2) in the worst case where S is the maximum set size, which is feasible for the stated bounds. Does not support other operators, non-integer operands, or sequences longer than 8 operands.
description: Interval dynamic programming over contiguous subexpressions. For each interval operands[i..j], dp[i][j] is the set of all integer values obtainable by fully parenthesizing that subexpression. Base intervals hold the single operand. For longer intervals, every split point k combines all values from the left interval with all values from the right interval using operators[k], adding results to a set to deduplicate. The answer is the cardinality of dp[0][n-1]. This exactly covers all full binary parenthesizations; partial parenthesizations yield values already represented by some full parenthesization under standard precedence, so the distinct-value set is unchanged. Python arbitrary-precision integers avoid overflow. Uncertainty is minimal; the only interpretive assumption is that inserting parentheses means all full parenthesizations, which is standard for this problem family.
